title: Sweeping Inverse Regularization Strength C and Plotting Test AUC
description: Train a StandardScaler + LogisticRegression(C=C) pipeline for each supplied C value and plot the test ROC AUC on a logarithmic x-axis.
source: draft: agy free model + edit: codex

steps.description: Define `Cs` with the supplied values and `aucs = []`, then loop over each `C`. Fit a `StandardScaler` and `LogisticRegression(C=C)` pipeline on `(X_train, y_train)` with the supplied iteration limit. Append `auc(fpr, tpr)` on `X_test`.
Plot `(Cs, aucs)` with circular markers, set a logarithmic horizontal scale with `plt.xscale("log")`, label the axes and title, and call `plt.show()`.
`Cs` steps by factors of `10` across four orders of magnitude. Thus, `plt.xscale("log")` spaces the five points evenly along the horizontal axis.

steps.question: In scikit-learn's `LogisticRegression(C=C)`, which supplied value in `Cs` applies the strongest regularization penalty to the weights?
steps.answer: The smallest supplied C value, because `C` is the inverse regularization strength ($1 / \lambda$), so smaller `C` means stronger regularization.
